dedupe_keys.name: a spatiotemporal natural human database to evaluate road development impacts in an amazon trinational frontier

description: A spatiotemporal natural-human database to evaluate road development impacts in an Amazon trinational frontier is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Geraldine Klarenberg et al. Road construction and paving bring socio-economic benefits to receiving regions but can also be drivers of deforestation and land cover change. Road infrastructure often increases migration and illegal economic activities, which in turn affect local hydrology, wildlife, vegetation structure and dynamics, and biodiversity. Coverage: not stated; published in 2019. Formats: CSV, GeoTIFF, Shapefile, Raster. The data are held in OSF and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked, and the coverage and resolution are those of the abstract only. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
